lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Thanks for joining. This is a practice round for the perception engineer role, so treat it like the real thing.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Sounds good, thanks for setting it up.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Can you start by telling me about your most recent perception project?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Sure. I led the obstacle detection stack for a sidewalk delivery robot. Our main detector ran at 30 FPS on the target hardware, and that was enough for the planner.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: What's your experience with TensorRT?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I converted our PyTorch models through ONNX into TensorRT engines, mostly FP16, and I experimented with INT8 calibration for the backbone.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Walk me through how you'd deploy a perception model on an edge device.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: First I profile the model on the device, then export to ONNX, build one engine per target, and keep preprocessing on the GPU so frames never bounce through host memory.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Our team uses CDTF for the camera pipeline, so you'd be working with it from day one.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I haven't used CDTF directly, but I've built similar multi-camera fusion pipelines.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: I'd like to hear about a time you dealt with a tight latency budget.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: On the delivery robot the end-to-end budget was 50 milliseconds from exposure to planner input. Honestly, we only got about 12 FPS on Orin at first, so we cut the input resolution and merged two detection heads.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: How did you measure that latency?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: We stamped every frame at capture and again when the detections were published, then tracked the p95 per release.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Why did you choose FP16 over INT8 for the final release?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: INT8 lost about two points of recall on small obstacles, and the safety review would not accept that.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Last one. Where do you want to grow in your next role?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I want to own the whole path from sensor calibration to on-vehicle deployment.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Great, that's everything from me. We'll send written feedback by email.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Let's settle the compute plan for the second robot prototype today.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Agreed. The perception stack has to run ROS 2 Humble with the CDTF camera nodes.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Jetson devices are hard to order and have a long lead time right now.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Then we should decide this week whether to wait for an Orin module or go with an x86 box and a discrete GPU.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: For the x86 option, the architecture is 16 GB RAM with a 1 TB SSD.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Is 16 GB enough if we record rosbags while the detector is running?

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Probably, as long as the SSD is NVMe and the bags go to a separate partition.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: What's the budget for the whole compute stack?

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Finance approved $40,000 for compute hardware this quarter.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: That leaves room for two units plus a spare.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Actually, I checked again and the cap is $25,000 including sensors.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: So we need to drop either the spare unit or the second lidar.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Which option keeps the CDTF calibration workflow intact?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Dropping the spare unit, because both lidars feed the calibration rig.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Okay, we decided to drop the spare and order one x86 unit now.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I'll own the purchase request and send the quote by Thursday.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Can you also check whether ROS 2 Jazzy supports our camera driver?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Yes, I'll test it on the bench next week.

selfQuestions: budget for the whole compute stack

title: Team standup with a ship-date change

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Morning everyone, quick standup. Let's start with blockers.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: The map tile service migration is done; the last integration test passed overnight.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Nice. Priya, are you still blocked on the label export?

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Yes, the export job times out after ten minutes on the large drives.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I can pair with her after standup. I think the batch size is too large.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Great, you own that. The plan is to ship the release on Friday.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Friday works if QA signs off by Thursday noon.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: We agreed the release notes go out with the build, and Marco will write them.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Who is updating the on-call rotation for release week?

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: I'll take that and post it in the team channel today.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: One change from the product side: we're moving the ship date to next Wednesday so the dashboard fix can land.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Okay, then the QA sign-off moves to Tuesday.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: What's the risk if the dashboard fix slips again?

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: Then we ship without it behind a feature flag.

lines.speaker: other
lines.text: Decided: feature flag fallback, ship next Wednesday, owners as discussed.

lines.speaker: self
lines.text: I'll update the tracker after this call.
